chapter: Rhythm and the Sam Morgan band
title: Personnel of the Morgan band and horn pairings
summary: He lists the Morgan band members, pianists May and George E. Parker, and discusses clarinet, soprano, alto and tenor combinations.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Can you tell us a bit more about the Sam or the Isaiah Morgan band? Who else was in that band when you joined?

Oh, they had, you see, Oyl Fushey, my nephew Sidney Brown, Andrew Morgan, Johnny Dave, Shine, Sam Morgan, Isaiah and myself. And we just knew that woman, May, Piano, May. Sometimes we used Piano, you know, May, May, Piano.
Who else did you use on Piano later?
Sometimes we used to use George E. Parker, you know, when May couldn't go to town, you know, we used George E. Parker.
Did you ever use clarinet much in that band?
Oh, yeah. Did Andrew double it? No, no. Yeah, Andrew used to play the clarinet and Oyl would play soprano. Oyl would play soprano.
Would there be any rule? Would they play those two together and then play alto and tenor together? Or would they play soprano and tenor?
No, they play together, understand? Like it's a special chorus like that, you know, they play for clarinet and sax, well, they play soprano, they play together, understand?
Would they play alto and clarinet at the same time?
No, they play alto and tenor.
That would sound better. Yeah, alto and tenor. Alto and tenor.
